answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent auditors prove the agent fabricated results. Auditors are randomly assigned and must also stake funds, so colluding identities cannot simply certify one another without risking capital. A meadow of cheap accounts may look large, but each needs locked funds and a reliable thread of honest work to earn trust; an opal-like reputation cannot be minted for free. The attacker pays upfront and loses stake when caught.
